title: America's trade war
hook: Since 2025 the United States has raised tariffs on almost every country. Eight chapters on what changed, who answered how, and who pays.
intro: In 2025 the United States raised its tariffs higher than at any time since the 1930s: first on its neighbours and China, then on almost every country at once, then on whole industries. This series follows it chapter by chapter, and is updated as the story moves.

dates.t: US adds 10% on all goods from China (fentanyl emergency)
25% on Canada and Mexico outside the USMCA; China raised to 20%
'Liberation Day': reciprocal tariffs announced for almost every country
Geneva truce: US–China rates cut to 30% and 10%
Court of International Trade rules the emergency tariffs unlawful
Steel and aluminium tariffs doubled to 50%
New country rates: 15% for the EU, Japan and South Korea; 39% Switzerland
India: 50% including a penalty for buying Russian oil
Trump and Xi meet in Busan: one-year truce
Supreme Court: the emergency law does not allow tariffs (6–3)
Emergency tariffs end; 10% surcharge for 150 days
Surcharge expires; Section 301 'forced labour' tariffs on 60 economies

title: Turkey: Anatolia, empire, republic
hook: Seven chapters across Anatolia, the Ottoman world and the republic, with dated sources and explicit map limits.
intro: This series follows Anatolia before the Ottomans, an imperial world, its collapse and the making and changing of the republic. It includes the Armenian genocide, compulsory population exchange and Kurdish histories. Contemporary material is a dated snapshot; each chapter states its coverage and mapping limits.

changelog.t: Four remaining chapters added, completing the seven-chapter reading order.

title: The Roman Empire
hook: Conquest, roads, frontiers and the separate endings of Roman rule in West and East.
intro: Seven chapters follow Rome and Carthage, imperial expansion, roads, shifting frontiers, division, western and eastern endpoints, and surviving places. Selected events and a nineteenth-century atlas interpretation provide historical geography with explicit source and precision limits.

changelog.t: Seven reviewed chapters registered, reusing All roads lead to Rome.

title: The United States
hook: Nine chapters on colonies, expansion, Indigenous dispossession, states, war, migration, elections and an overseas role.
intro: Located events and cited schematic movements follow territorial acquisition and Indigenous land loss as separate histories. Modern state geography provides an explicitly disclosed comparison frame for statehood, Civil War categories and election results. The final chapter follows selected historical overseas acquisitions and NATO, with no current troop totals claimed.

changelog.t: Nine chapters registered; America abroad revised to sourced historical overseas acquisitions and NATO.

title: The European Union
hook: Six chapters on enlargement, overlapping clubs, budget flows, regions, Brexit and candidates.
intro: Dated membership maps trace enlargement and show how the EU, euro area and Schengen overlap. A defined 2021–2025 budget comparison distinguishes ordinary allocations, recovery spending and national financing. Selected regional GDP observations are separate from nationally allocated cohesion money. Modern outlines and region reference points have explicit geographic limits.

changelog.t: Six reviewed chapters added, including dated memberships and fixed historical data windows.

title: The war in Ukraine
hook: Seven chapters from Crimea and Donbas through invasion, changing fighting, energy disruption and displacement.
intro: Dated events and UCDP observations describe selected geographic patterns without reconstructing continuous fronts or asserting military control. The series distinguishes the UN account of legal status from the basemap’s orientation conventions. Its source windows stop in August 2026 for UCDP events, end-2025 for refugee stocks and May 2022 for the NASA Kyiv imagery; this is a dated account, not a live front map.

changelog.t: Seven reviewed chapters added with explicit, separate observation windows.

title: World War II
hook: Eight chapters on the war’s geography, occupation, campaigns, civilian harm and aftermath.
intro: Dated national occupation-status comparisons, diplomatic border observations, original cited event locators and selected campaign movement have distinct meanings. A cleared US Army atlas supplies a western overview; its Pacific scan describes Allied commands. Atrocity accounts use plain language and static, sourced locations rather than competitive or decorative animation.

changelog.t: Complete scoped chapter order registered after chapter source and visual review.

title: The Holy Roman Empire
hook: Six chapters on imperial institutions, fragmented territories, Westphalia and dissolution.
intro: The series connects selected imperial places and primary institutional texts with an explicitly coarse circa-1789 outline and selected Habsburg/Brandenburg holdings extracted from a creator-licensed reconstruction. A separately dated 1796 atlas scan supplies readable territorial patchwork. Neither source is a surveyed boundary or an exhaustive account of hundreds of imperial states.

changelog.t: Complete scoped chapter order registered after chapter source and visual review.
